note: Week of 2026-09-28 build. Run fired on schedule Sunday 9/27 ~9:00pm CT; entries are recorded at official SIP regular-session closes of Friday 2026-09-25 (connected brokerage market-data feed) and open Monday 9/28. PRIOR WEEK (9/21-9/25) realized +$1,804.28 (+2.46%), 8 of 11 names green: AMAT +9.09% (+566.02) and MU +6.54% (+465.36) led as the memory/equipment trade extended; UAL +4.86%, ETN +3.58%, WDC +3.50%, ISRG +3.01%, LLY +2.65%, GEV +1.84%. CME -4.18% (-265.19) was the only real loss; GS -0.70%, HOOD -0.35%. Capital rolled forward to $75,294.03. New book: 10 names, $64,369.70 deployed (85.5%), cash $10,924.33. Carried forward: MU, ETN, GEV, LLY, ISRG (re-entered at 9/25 closes). EARNINGS INSIDE THE WINDOW: MU fiscal Q4 Wed 9/30 after close (binary; sized 8.6%). Macro: 10-year hit 5.225% last week (highest since 2007), 30-year 5.50%; Brent ~$105-106 Sunday night after Trump rejected Iran's ceasefire conditions; US-China Board of Trade details due Mon 9/28 (medical devices, ag); consumer confidence Tue, jobs data late week; S&P 500 futures -0.2% Sunday evening. Themes: AI-semis momentum into Micron (MU, AMD), rotation into mega-cap AI platforms (MSFT Copilot relaunch + Stifel upgrade, META Muse), AI power (ETN, BE, GEV), healthcare with dated catalysts (HUM Star ratings ~10/8, ISRG China device access, LLY). Zero energy, zero financials by design; AMAT/WDC profits booked.

positions.name: Micron Technology
positions.catalyst: Held over from last week (+6.54%) and re-entered at Friday 9/25's official close of $1,082.28, this time WITH the event inside the window: fiscal Q4 results post Wednesday 9/30 after the close. Guidance was $49-51B revenue, $30-32 non-GAAP EPS and ~86% gross margin; consensus sits at ~$31.50 EPS on ~$51.2B. Micron has beaten decisively on each of the last several reports, HBM supply for 2026 is fully booked, HBM4 is shipping into Nvidia's Vera Rubin, and RBC's datapoint that calendar-Q3 DRAM contract prices ran up more than 20% q/q (vs ~10% forecast) points to upside on the fiscal-Q1 guide, which is what the stock will trade on.
positions.risks: This is now a binary: a ~24% sequential EPS step-up is the bar and the stock is up ~540% over twelve months, so an in-line print or a cautious FQ1 guide can take 10%+ off in one session. $1.22T market cap means the whole AI-semis complex (AMD in this book) moves with the reaction. Still 13.8% below the $1,255 June high, so the market has not fully re-rated.
positions.driver: The single biggest scheduled catalyst of the week in the strongest earnings trend in the market, sized just below the top tier (8.6%) because it is a binary event.

positions.name: Advanced Micro Devices
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 9/25 at $630.63 after printing a new 52-week high of $639.00 intraday - up from $559.82 the prior Friday (+12.6% on the week) and from $456 at the start of September. Monday 9/21 was the breakout: +9.9% on 44.5M shares vs a ~21M 30-day average (2.1x). Bank of America's Vivek Arya then raised his target to $720 from $620 (Buy) on 9/25, 14% above the entry. It is the cleanest price-momentum chart in large-cap semis, at a new high with no overhead supply.
positions.risks: 161.8x trailing earnings - there is no valuation support if the AI trade wobbles, and Micron's Wednesday print is a sympathy risk in both directions. Buying at a fresh 52-week high after a 38% run in four weeks is the definition of extended; a failed follow-through can retrace quickly.
positions.driver: Pure momentum confirmed by a fresh target hike, at a new high with zero overhead resistance.

positions.name: Microsoft
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 9/25 at $516.17, +3.7% on the day and +4.5% on the week, on 38.2M shares against a 22.1M 30-day average (1.73x) - the heaviest relative volume of any mega-cap. Two fresh catalysts: Stifel upgraded to Buy from Hold on 9/23 with a $575 target (+11%), citing Azure strength and Copilot passing 30 million paid seats; then on 9/25 Microsoft relaunched the Copilot app with full Word/Excel/PowerPoint inside it, a new Home surface integrating Chat and agentic Cowork, and natural-language coding tools. Commentary Friday framed the Mag 7 as 'back en vogue' as money rotates from the extended AI-buildout names into cash-flow compounders.
positions.risks: Still 6.8% below the $553.72 high of October 2025, so it is recovering rather than leading. A one-day 3.7% gap on a product launch can be sold if Monday's tape is risk-off on oil/yields (10-year at 5.2%). No scheduled event inside the window; earnings are late October.
positions.driver: Upgrade plus product launch plus 1.7x volume in a $3.8T name - the rotation-into-quality leg of the book.

positions.name: Meta Platforms
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 9/25 at $751.66, +12.9% on the week and roughly +30% in September - on pace for its biggest monthly gain since July 2013 - after the Muse AI agent became the top free iOS app (~730K downloads in its first five days) and was showcased at Connect. Monday 9/21 was +11.3% on 48.7M shares (2.1x average). The sell side followed: JPMorgan raised its target to $920 (from $820) calling Muse potentially 'the most widely used consumer AI application since ChatGPT', Piper Sandler to $875 (from $785), Wells Fargo to $796. 47 of 54 analysts rate it Buy.
positions.risks: Friday was a -3.3% reversal off Thursday's $779.82 record, and Sunday evening it indicated ~$738 in overnight trading - so the week may open with profit-taking. Adoption data for a new app is noisy and the move is already 30% in a month.
positions.driver: The strongest fresh fundamental narrative in mega-cap tech, bought on the first pullback from a record rather than at the high.

positions.name: Eaton Corp.
positions.catalyst: Carried forward after +3.58% last week, re-entered at Friday 9/25's $439.98 close. On 9/25 Eaton signed an agreement to acquire COL Group from Oaktree, expanding manufacturing capacity for data-center and utility markets in EMEA, adding to the $242M Arkansas Fibrebond expansion announced 9/2. Management has raised 2026 organic growth to as much as 12% with data-center orders up ~85%; 28 analysts rate it Buy, none Sell, consensus target ~$502 (+14%). Higher highs three weeks running off the 9/14 low of $387.
positions.risks: 44.8x earnings is a growth multiple on a cyclical business; with the 10-year at 5.2% and the Fed hawkish, long-duration industrials are rate-sensitive. Still 8% below the $478 August high. Correlated with BE and GEV on any AI-capex de-rating.
positions.driver: Steady momentum plus a fresh capacity-building acquisition - the lowest-volatility way to own AI power in the book.

positions.name: Bloom Energy
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 9/25 at $288.70, +8.3% on the day on 17.4M shares, after Oracle publicly REAFFIRMED its 2.4-gigawatt fuel-cell agreement following a force-majeure notice that had knocked the stock down on 9/24. That removes the week's biggest overhang. BE also joined the S&P 500 at the open on 9/21 (replacing Molson Coors), latest quarter revenue ~$1.07B (+166% y/y) with product revenue +215%, and its 800V DC-native platform is pitched as a way for hyperscalers to bypass grid interconnection queues.
positions.risks: The force-majeure notice itself signals real schedule risk on the Project Jupiter permits even with Oracle reaffirming. 393x earnings and a stock up ~230% YTD make this the highest-beta name in the book, 18% below its June high. Sized in the lower tier (8.4%) for that reason.
positions.driver: Overhang removed by the customer itself, confirmed by an 8% volume day - a high-beta AI-power satellite, deliberately sized small.

positions.name: GE Vernova
positions.catalyst: Carried forward after +1.84% last week, re-entered at $957.63. CEO Scott Strazik reiterated on 9/24 that the backlog (US$176B at Q2) is tracking to US$200B very early in 2027, with second-half commitments running above prior 20 GW guidance. The stock has made higher weekly closes three weeks running off the 9/14 low ($868), and gas turbines remain the only dispatchable baseload hyperscalers can order today. Earnings 10/21 are outside the window.
positions.risks: The weakest fresh catalyst in the book - the backlog number is a restatement, and the stock fell 1.3% on the day it was repeated. 20% below its $1,196 July high. Third industrial on the same AI-power thesis alongside ETN and BE.
positions.driver: Kept as the AI-power ballast with order-book visibility, sized in the bottom tier because its catalyst is repetition rather than news.

positions.name: Humana
positions.catalyst: Closed Friday 9/25 at $397.93, +7.7% on the day on 1.94M shares vs a 0.96M 30-day average (2.0x), after Barclays' Andrew Mok upgraded to Overweight from Equal Weight and lifted the target to $515 from $407 (+29%). The thesis is the Medicare Advantage Star ratings due ~October 8: Barclays sees ~75% odds that contract H5216 (2.4M members) moves back to bonus status for the BY28 cycle. Pre-announcement positioning typically builds through the week before the release.
positions.risks: The ratings themselves land AFTER this window, so the position rides anticipation, not the answer. Managed care is policy-sensitive (CMS rates, MA scrutiny) and the stock is still 7% below its July high after a violent round-trip from a $163 March low.
positions.driver: A fresh upgrade with a big target and a dated catalyst just beyond the window - the setup where positioning does the work during the hold.

positions.name: Eli Lilly
positions.catalyst: Carried forward after +2.65% last week, re-entered at $1,183.46 near a 14-month high trend. Fresh news flow: FDA approved Onswik, a once-weekly basal insulin for type 2 diabetes, on 9/24, and Lilly signed an InnoCare research/licensing deal worth up to $3.35B in milestones. GLP-1 share gains continue. The weekly chart shows a higher close three weeks running ($1,116 -> $1,153 -> $1,183).
positions.risks: 40x earnings; drug-pricing headlines under this administration are unpredictable; 8.4% below the August high. No scheduled event in the window.
positions.driver: The book's low-correlation anchor, still trending up and freshly supported by an FDA approval.

positions.name: Intuitive Surgical
positions.catalyst: Carried forward after +3.01% last week, re-entered at $405.18 - closing at the week's high after a third straight up week off the $328.57 July low. New catalyst: USTR Greer said 9/25 the US and China reached agreements giving preferential treatment to a subset of goods including US MEDICAL DEVICES, with 'a lot more details' due Monday 9/28. China tenders have been Intuitive's weakest region (local suppliers winning), so any preferential access is incremental. 24 of 32 analysts rate it Buy.
positions.risks: The trade details may prove narrow or exclude robotic surgery systems; the stock is still 33% below its January high on slowing da Vinci procedure growth (13.5-15.5% guide). 46x earnings.
positions.driver: A recovering trend with a specific, dated policy catalyst on Monday morning.
